cookies.title: YouTube cookies
cookies.description: The recommended way to sign in to YouTube. The app takes cookies from a browser where you're already signed in: your password never goes into PeekyCat, and YouTube sees a regular sign-in from your browser. Both yt-dlp and the built-in downloader use them.
cookies.steps_title: How to get and add cookies
cookies.step_1: Install a browser extension that exports cookies in the Netscape format: “Get cookies.txt LOCALLY” for Chrome, Edge, Yandex Browser and other Chromium browsers, or “cookies.txt” for Firefox. Allow it to run in private windows.
cookies.step_2: Open a new private (incognito) window: Ctrl+Shift+N in Chrome, Edge and Yandex Browser or Ctrl+Shift+P in Firefox; on macOS use Cmd instead of Ctrl. Sign in to your account on youtube.com.
cookies.step_3: In the same window, open a new tab, close the YouTube tab and go to youtube.com/robots.txt — it must be the only tab of the window. This keeps YouTube from rotating the cookies while you save them.
cookies.step_4: Click the extension icon and export the cookies of the current site (youtube.com) to a .txt file.
cookies.step_5: Close the private window right away without signing out: signing out or browsing on in that window invalidates the saved cookies.
cookies.step_6: Click “Choose cookies.txt…” below and pick the saved file.
cookies.refresh: Cookies don't last forever, and YouTube may reset them sooner. If “confirm you're not a bot” or a message about expired cookies shows up again, repeat the steps and choose the new file: it replaces the old one.
cookies.guide: Detailed guide in the yt-dlp FAQ
cookies.warning: The cookies file gives access to your account: don't share it with anyone.
cookies.sign_in_window_active: You're signed in with Google in the app window now. We recommend replacing it with cookies: importing them replaces that sign-in.
cookies.success: Cookies imported: signed in to YouTube.
